editorial:
Imagine being locked in a cell and knowing you are going to die, but having no idea when the guards will come for you. That is the scary setup of this movie. You follow four men who are all cold-hearted killers, so you aren't exactly rooting for them to get away with it. However, the movie isn't trying to make them look like good guys. Instead, it focuses on the cruel way the government handles the death penalty in France. The vibe is heavy and stressful because you feel the panic of these men as they wait for the blade of the guillotine to drop.

The acting is great because the actors make you feel the raw fear of the condemned. While the pacing is slow at times, it makes the ending feel even more shocking. If you like dramas that make you think about right and wrong, you should definitely check this out. Since it is an older film, you might want to find a restored version.
endingExplained: The movie ends with the four men finally being led to the guillotine. It shows the brutal reality of the execution process, where the men are dragged away without any warning. By showing the cold, mechanical way the state kills them, the film argues that the government is just as much of a murderer as the criminals. It wraps up by leaving you feeling shaken and questioning if the death penalty is actually justice.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves legal dramas and stories about social justice.
